Agad na kinumpuni ng Quezon City Government, sa pangunguna ng Department of Engineering, ang lumang inlet sa bahagi ng Mapagsangguni corner Madasalin St. sa Brgy. Sikatuna Village. Naglagay rin ng karagdagang suporta upang masiguro ang tibay at kaligtasan nito.

Bilang dagdag na hakbang para sa kaligtasan ng publiko, pinaplano na ang pagsasaayos ng sidewalk sa lugar para maiwasang maglakad ang mga pedestrian sa mismong kalsada.

Patuloy ang Quezon City Government sa pagsasagawa ng inspeksyon at pagkukumpuni ng mga imprastraktura sa lungsod upang maiwasan ang anumang  aksidente.

Hinihikayat din natin ang publiko na ireport sa amin o sa Helpline 122 ang mga kahalintulad na concern.

Maraming salamat po.

Members of Kilusang Bayan Kontra Kurakot announce plans to hold an anti-corruption rally on February 25, in time for the 40th anniversary of the EDSA People Power revolution, during a press conference in Quezon City on Monday, January 19.

The protest aims to call on the administration to detain high-ranking elected officials implicated in large-scale corruption cases, particularly public officials and contractors involved in flood-control anomalies.

📷: Santi San Juan | MB

As the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee resumed its hearing on the alleged flood control anomaly, progressive groups led by Sanlakas staged a protest at the Senate of the Philippines on Monday, January 19.

Joined by the Philippine Alliance of Human Rights Advocates (PAHRA), Philippine Movement for Climate Justice (PMCJ), Partido Lakas ng Masa (PLM), Bukluran ng Manggagawang Pilipino (BMP), and Samahan ng Mamamayan–Zone One Tondo Organization (SM-ZOTO), the demonstrators criticized what they called the failure of existing accountability mechanisms to go after the “big fish.”

📷: Mark Balmores | MB
